irr_f01_reservation_adapter_note: api/irrigation_reservation_adapter.py: IRR-F01 DB adapter contract binding the pure reservation kernel to the platform-owned v195 tables + the EXISTING execution-request/outbox path via an injected ExecutionRequestPort. Lock-before-evaluate reserve-and-request-dispatch inside the caller's tx (set tenant GUC -> ordered advisory locks -> fresh overlap read + admission -> INSERT evaluation -> INSERT reservations+events -> outbox intent). Committed reservation = dispatch_requested; actuator receipt = dispatched. Forward compensation on post-commit actuator failure (reservation->cancelled, request->dispatch_failed), no rollback. No new execution SoR; no new route. Live execution + the port's outbox binding are the deferred Phase-4 PostgreSQL integration gate.
irr_f01_execution_request_port_note: api/irrigation_execution_request_port.py: IRR-F01 Gate B — the real ExecutionRequestPort binding the reservation adapter to the EXISTING emit_event outbox on the same tx connection (dispatch_requested intent, entity_type='operation' to satisfy the events CHECK; the outbox worker + decision-service do the live delivery). Registers EventType IRRIGATION_RESERVATION_DISPATCH_REQUESTED/_FAILED. Certified live (Gate B1): emit atomicity + rollback + compensation on PostgreSQL 16.

capability_plan_ci7_ci9_note: 666->672: capability-plan increment. TWO modules are wired into a production path and earn platform ownership on the same terms as the entries above: core/crop_intelligence/canonical_inputs.py (CI-7) is called from crop_intelligence/engine.py so phenology reads GDD from CanonicalWeatherState instead of legacy scalars, failing closed on a malformed state; core/crop_intelligence/policy_engine.py (CI-9) replaces the hardcoded stress-flag if-chain in that same engine with versioned policy packs, and is what makes the crop engine generic. Both are platform-owned because Crop Intelligence itself is platform-owned and boundary-locked by scripts/ci/crop_intelligence_boundary_gate.py. FOUR modules are NOT yet wired and are recorded as such rather than justified as production code: core/canonical_field_state.py, core/yield_intelligence.py, core/equipment_intelligence.py and core/economic_scenarios.py are pure, tested cores with ZERO non-test consumers - no route, no persistence, no production caller. By the INT-004 precedent that is groundwork, not an integration lifecycle. They are admitted to the baseline so the capability-plan increment can land intact, NOT because they have earned platform concentration; the honest alternative is relocating them to owner services once each acquires a real consumer. Tracked as CAPABILITY-CORES-NOT-WIRED in sahool-brain/gaps/registry.md. No new route: p2_6 domain budget unchanged at 626 <= 629.
ci10_knowledge_layer_note: 672->673: CI-10 governed crop-knowledge layer, admitted on ONE ground only - it has a production consumer. core/crop_intelligence/canonical_inputs.py resolves crop thermal knowledge through core/crop_intelligence/knowledge_layer.py instead of calling core.crop_cards.loader directly, so the engine emits knowledge_provenance (digest + source_ids) and reports canonical_input_sources.crop_knowledge as governed_knowledge_layer or unavailable, failing closed into governed_crop_knowledge_unavailable rather than silently substituting a default. The CI-11 learning engine and the Agricultural OS composer were deliberately NOT admitted in this slice: both exist and pass their own tests, but neither has a non-test consumer, and admitting a module with zero production consumption would make this ratchet a witness to files that exist rather than capabilities in use. Each will be admitted only in the same PR that adds its production consumer plus a guard proving it. No new route: p2_6 domain budget unchanged at 626 <= 629.
field_state_producers_missing_01_soil_no: 673->674: api/canonical_soil_state.py (FIELD-STATE-PRODUCERS-MISSING-01, soil half). Has a production consumer on the same terms as INT-004: api/routers/internal_service.py's _compose_canonical() calls resolve_canonical_soil_state() to fill the soil= argument to core.canonical_field_state.compose_canonical_field_state instead of a hardcoded None. It is an httpx client (soil_hydraulic_client.py's pattern) that reads soil-service's GET /v1/fields/{field_id}/soil/profile and normalizes the response's contract_version key into schema_version, which is what the core's schema check reads; never synthesizes a profile on any failure, 404, or missing token. No new route: platform route budget unchanged. Weather stays unwired in this slice - see the gap registry entry for why.
field_state_producers_missing_01_spectra: 674->675: api/canonical_spectral_state.py (FIELD-STATE-PRODUCERS-MISSING-01, spectral half). Same terms as the soil half: a production consumer on an existing route, no new route, no synthesis. api/routers/internal_service.py's _compose_canonical() calls resolve_canonical_spectral_state() to fill the spectral= argument to core.canonical_field_state.compose_canonical_field_state instead of a hardcoded None. It is not new logic: the server-side resolver already existed inside api/routers/crop_twin.py and was moved here unchanged, because a resolver reachable from exactly one router is why this composer declared spectral_missing for fields whose indices the platform could already read. Both consumers now share it; crop_twin imports the name so its existing monkeypatch-based tests keep working. NDVI is the master index: without it the resolver returns None rather than a product whose indices are all None, which would set availability.spectral=true while nothing is known. spectral is not in the core's required=(weather,water,soil), so wiring it cannot raise operational_eligible - locked by tests/test_canonical_field_state_wiring.py::test_wiring_spectral_cannot_raise_eligibility_on_its_own. Weather stays unwired - see the gap registry entry for the measured reason.
canonical_phenology_state_note: 675->676: api/canonical_phenology_state.py, admitted on the one ground this file accepts since ci10_knowledge_layer_note - it has a production consumer, added in the SAME change with a guard proving it. api/routers/phenology.py::field_phenology calls build_canonical_phenology_state under ?canonical=true; before this, GET /api/v1/fields/{field_id}/phenology derived current_stage from calendar age alone (current_stage(crop_id, days_after_sowing)) and presented that guess with nothing marking it as a guess - a recorded observation could not change it, and two trusted disagreeing observations produced the same answer as agreement. The module separates observed from predicted, lets a recent trusted field observation be authoritative, and blocks on conflict. NO NEW ROUTE (the INT-004A precedent): it folds into the existing GET as an opt-in parameter defaulting to False, so the existing response is byte-identical - locked by tests/test_canonical_phenology_wiring.py, which is falsified on four plants (builder not called, router deciding a status itself, GDD laundered from wofost_seasons, opt-in flipped to default). Honest limit recorded in the router docstring: accumulated_gdd is passed None, because canonical GDD is weather-engine-owned and needs a daily temperature series this endpoint does not hold, and wofost_seasons.gdd_accumulated is simulation output - passing it would launder a simulation as measured heat. First wiring slice of CAPABILITY-WAVE-V217-V231-DEFERRED; the other thirteen modules stay out of this baseline until each earns the same proof.
